1.1: 1.1 And King David was old. JEROME, letter to Nepotian, volume 1. Does it not seem to you, if you follow the letter that kills, to be a fiction or the playthings of the Atellan farces? A cold old man is wrapped in garments and does not grow warm unless by the embrace of a young girl. Bathsheba was still alive, etc., down to and Rahab the harlot, in type of the Church, hung out the cord containing the mystery of blood, that Jericho perishing her house might be saved, whence of the saints it is said: These are they who came from the warmth of the house of Rechab, I Chronicles 2. And elsewhere: I came to send fire on the earth, Luke 12., etc., which being kindled in the hearts of the disciples compelled them to say: Was not our heart burning within us? ibid., 24. And when he was covered, etc. David suffered excessive cold, either because he was born of aged parents, or because he had shed much blood in battle, or rather from when he saw the angel striking the people he wasted away with violent fear, whence in the discomfort of cold he remained until death.
1.5: 1.5 But Adonijah. He signifies the Jewish people, who seems to be the elder son, because it first received the law, and despising the Gentile people, which by the grace of God was called later, thought that it alone reigned with the Lord. For Adonijah is interpreted lord ruler. But the people of the Church, with the true Solomon, that is our peaceful one, whose body it is, by divine ordinance is put into the kingdom, from which deservedly for unfaithfulness the elder son, that is the first people, is cast down.
2.5: 2.5 You also. David commanded Solomon about the just retribution of those who were a comfort to him, or who unjustly harmed him, whom he himself patiently bore. And the prophecy indicates what evil or good must happen in the future, which the true Solomon will fulfill. Meanwhile the patience of God often permits the good to be tried and the wicked to enjoy delights.
2.19: 2.19 Bathsheba therefore came to the king. RABANUS. Adonijah, with Bathsheba interceding, etc., down to nor the law, which the Jews suppose to be a helper for them before God.
2.36: 2.36 And you shall not go out, etc. The true Solomon commands us who dwell in Jerusalem never to go out. But if those once subject to us flee, let us not therefore go out to follow the tracks of the fugitives, lest while we wish to save the fleeing we ourselves perish, but rather let the dead bury the dead, and the eye, the hand, the foot that scandalizes, while there is time, let us pluck out and cut off from us.
3.4: 3.4 Solomon therefore went. In Gibeon was the greatest high place, where was the tabernacle which Moses made, and the bronze altar, on which Solomon offering a thousand victims merited a divine oracle.
3.14: 3.14 And if you walk in my ways, etc. Without keeping the commandments of God, no one can obtain long days, that is blessedness. GREGORY, Moralia book VIII, chapter 17. After the Lord illumines the darkness of our error with the light of his knowledge, etc., down to that we may be reformed to the substance of the promised incorruption. JEROME, letter 131, volume 1. Some suppose that this is to be understood of the Synagogue and the Church, etc., down to note also what the Church says against the Synagogue.
3.17: 3.17 I and this woman. Because after the resurrection of the Savior one was gathered from both peoples. He elegantly added: I gave birth in the room with her. For the Church from the Gentiles, which did not have the law and the prophets, gave birth in the house of the synagogue, and did not go out of the room, but went in. Hence: The king brought me into his chamber, Song of Songs 2. And: I will bring you into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her who conceived me, ibid., 3. RABANUS. If you consider Pilate washing his hands and saying: I am innocent of the blood of this just man, Matthew 27, and the centurion confessing: Truly this was the Son of God, Mark 15, and those who before the passion desire through Philip to see the Lord, you do not doubt that the Church first gave birth; and afterward the people of the Jews was born, for whom the Lord prayed: Father, forgive them, etc., and three thousand believed in one day and another five thousand. GREGORY. By nursing mothers the order of teachers, etc., down to they themselves receive their children whole and living, when in the supreme judgment they obtain from their life a perfect retribution.
3.19: 3.19 Dead. RABANUS. For while it follows the observance of the law and joins the grace of the Gospel to the law, it was covered with the error of darkness.
3.20: 3.20 She took my son. Living, namely: not to possess him but to kill him. For she did not do this out of love for the son, but out of hatred of her rival.
3.21: 3.21 And looking at him more carefully, etc. RABANUS. It is long to show how through Paul and other ecclesiastical men the Church understood that he was not her son, who was feared in the law, and in the light knew him whom she did not see in the darkness. The two women, one of whom burned with love, in the other pretense crept in, figure the Church and the Synagogue or heretical perversity, each of which kills even her own by nourishing them wickedly, and persuades others by enticing them until she destroys them. Between the two women the Lord, while he settles with the spirit of his mouth what is just, restores to each what is due.
3.24: 3.24 He said therefore. RABANUS. Pretending ignorance, he measures human feelings by the dispensation of the flesh, as also there: Where have you laid him? John 20. And elsewhere: Who touched me? Luke 8.
3.25: 3.25 Divide. THE SAME. The Lord tests nature by nature, and wishes according to the will of each to divide the living son between law and grace: not that he approves, but he says he wishes it to rebuke the calumny of the Synagogue.
3.26: 3.26 But she said. THE SAME. The Church, which knows he is hers, willingly yields to her rival that he may live at least with her, lest, divided between law and grace, he be struck by the sword of Christ, hence: Behold, I Paul say to you, that if you keep the law, Christ will profit you nothing, Galatians 5.
4.22: 4.22 The food of Solomon. RABANUS. The refreshment of Christ, who is fed by right faith and good works, which are daily offered to him by the Catholic Church.
4.23: 4.23 Twenty oxen. THE SAME. The preachers of the New Testament, who have in themselves as it were a doubled Decalogue, when they preach the New and Old Testaments equally, full of love of God and neighbor. Besides venison. By the hunting of diverse animals are meant those who from diverse nations are daily caught by the nets of the Gospel through spiritual hunters, and are brought to the feeding of the Savior.
4.26: 4.26 Forty, etc. By forty are designated the times of the ancient law, which Moses, about to receive it, fasted forty days, and the people who were instructed by it were forty years in the desert. And twelve. This number signifies the present time, in which the apostolic teaching nourishes the people of the New Testament.
4.28: 4.28 Barley, etc. Lest anything be lacking in the house of the king, the order of preachers labors in writing and speaking, that it may abound at the table of the Lord, from which the faithful are nourished.
4.32: 4.32 And his songs were. It is agreed that neither the songs nor the disputations of Solomon exist today. Five thousand. On account of the five senses, which he who rules well in various virtues is blessed, and through them as it were sings five thousand songs to the Lord.
4.33: 4.33 Hyssop. RABANUS. Hyssop, a lowly herb clinging to the rock, etc., down to then indeed he bowed the cedar, that is the arrogance of the world, to the humility of hyssop, that is to the foolishness of the cross. And he discoursed. THE SAME. For all things are naked and open to Christ, Hebrews 4. And he disputes when he sets before us the reason of each in his Scriptures, and makes manifest the sacraments which were hidden from ages and generations, that we may consider the blessedness of angels, the usefulness of men, the cunning of demons, and rejecting what is evil, pursue what is good.
5.3: 5.3 And that he could not build a house, etc. BEDE, Questions on the Books of Kings. The house that Solomon built was a figure of the Church, etc., down to in some it shows the struggles of men rewarded with the angels. THE SAME, book on the Temple of Solomon, chapter 1. This spiritual house is also signified by the tabernacle made in the desert, etc., down to and in many ways shows and figures the salvation of all the nations in Christ.
5.6: 5.6 Command therefore that they cut for me, etc. RABANUS. The servants of Hiram cutting cedars for Solomon from Lebanon, etc., down to they knew the errors of the Gentiles better, and therefore overcame them more skillfully. For you know that there is no man among my people who knows how to cut wood, etc. BEDE, as above. First we must speak of the workmen of the temple, who or whence they were, and of the material itself, etc., down to wheat, namely of the word of God, the oil of charity, of anointing and of the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit.
5.10: 5.10 So Hiram gave Solomon cedar wood and fir wood, according to all, etc. Tyre, whence King Hiram, is an island given to trade, where were the best workers in wood, who gave precious timber receiving food. For they live not by tilling the field but by trading. There is Mount Lebanon, from whose trees the house of the Lord was made. Hence Lebanon also is said there: Open, Lebanon, your gates, Zechariah 11.
5.13: 5.13 And King Solomon chose. BEDE, as above, chapter 3. Not in vain did he choose workmen from all Israel, etc., down to in which the minds of the faithful are regarded by the Lord by daily illumination as the moon by the sun. Workmen from all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men. These workmen were proselytes. Their masters were from the Jews, because he did not make anyone of Israel serve.
5.14: 5.14 Adoniram was over this levy. BEDE, ibid. My lord is exalted. This is Christ, who is set over the workmen of the temple, etc., down to that by prayers and fasts it may be worthy of the heavenly inspector and visitor.
5.15: 5.15 And Solomon had seventy thousand who carried burdens, and eighty thousand stonecutters on the mountain. BEDE, ibid. Nor is it to be passed over that the seventy and eighty thousand of burden-bearers and stonecutters with their overseers were not Israelites, etc., down to Some endowed with both virtues come together to the work of the house of the Lord; hence: Rebuke the unquiet, comfort the fainthearted, etc., I Thessalonians 5. Stonecutters. BEDE, ibid. Stonecutters are cutters of stones, etc., down to because rescued from the power of darkness we have come to the citadel of virtues which is in the unity of the Church.
5.16: 5.16 Besides the overseers. The overseers are the makers of sacred Scripture by whose teaching we are trained to teach the ignorant, rebuke the scornful, and bear one another's burdens. Of three thousand. On account of the faith of the Trinity, which the holy words preach. That in Chronicles three thousand six hundred are written, looks to their perfection. For six, in which the adornment of the world was completed, signifies the perfect works of good: and because holy Scripture teaches works of righteousness to be had with faith in truth, rightly the overseers of the works of the temple were three thousand six hundred.
5.17: 5.17 And the king commanded that they take. BEDE, ibid. To build the house of the Lord, first wood and stones are cut from the mountain, etc., down to hence: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Ephesians 2. Great stones. BEDE, ibid., chapter 4. Or the precious stones, great, squared, are the first teachers, who heard the word of salvation from the Lord himself. The layers of stones or wood placed above are the following priests or teachers, by whose preaching the Church grows and is adorned with virtues. RABANUS from Bede. Of what color were the stones, etc., down to the white marble from which the house of the elect is built signifies clean action and conscience chastened from every blemish of corruption; hence: Let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement, etc., II Corinthians 7. For the foundation of the temple. BEDE, ibid. The foundation is Christ, etc., down to that, having cast away superfluous words, deeds, and thoughts, they may become worthy to bear the burden of the Church.
5.18: 5.18 And the Giblites prepared the timber and the stones. RABANUS from Bede, ibid. Gebal is a city of Phoenicia, etc., down to he builds not a sanctuary for the Lord but ruin for himself, who presumes to teach what he has not himself learned. To build the house. THE SAME, ibid. After the foundation composed of such, the house is to be built with the prepared timber and stones, set in order, which have been drawn from their place, because after the first rudiments of faith, after the foundations of humility laid in us by the example of lofty men, the wall of good works must be added upward, and, with courses of stones set upon one another, we must advance from virtue to virtue.
6.1: 6.1 It came to pass therefore. RABANUS from Bede, book on the Temple of Solomon, chapter 5. A commemoration is made of the going out from Egypt, etc., down to nor Scripture which would intimate the grace of the New Testament in the Old. In the fourth year. In the fourth year of King Solomon the house began to be built: because after the dispensation of the incarnation of Christ, written in the four Gospels, was fulfilled, with the Holy Spirit sent, the structure of the Church began. In the month Zif, which is the same month. BEDE, ibid. That in the second month, etc., down to whence it is clear that as soon as Passover was done he began to build the house of the Lord, and the people, consecrated by the mystical solemnity, put hands to the mystical work. He began to build. THE SAME, ibid. Where the temple was built is made clear in Chronicles, etc., down to but of the interior peace which she had with her Maker she was made possessor. What David had prepared, etc. For David had prepared by singing psalms, other prophets prepared by prophesying a place for the Lord: namely for the true Solomon, in which he would build a house, because they established the hearts of hearers in faith, urging that they should receive with faithful devotion the incarnate Son of God. Hence: Lift up your eyes and see the regions, for they are already white for the harvest: and he who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, that he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together, John 4. That he says: Lift up your eyes and see the place that is prepared for building the house, and he who builds by teaching receives wages and gathers precious stones for eternal life: that he who prepares the place for the building and he who builds, that is the prophet foretelling the one to come and the apostle preaching the Lord who has come, may together obtain one reward. In length, etc. The length of the house signifies the longsuffering of the Church, by which she patiently bears adversity until she reaches the homeland. This is of sixty cubits, because six signifies the perfection of good works; because we ought by longsuffering so to bear adversity that through good works we may merit to enter the promised homeland. Twenty cubits. On account of the twofold distance of charity, by which we love God and neighbor. In breadth. Breadth signifies charity, which with enlarged bosom of the mind loves friends in God and enemies for God's sake until, with them converted to peace or wholly destroyed, it rejoices in the Lord with friends alone. BEDE, ibid. Note that the thirty cubits of height did not reach up to the roof of the temple, but to the lower upper room. For it is plainly written in Chronicles that the height was one hundred twenty cubits, about the mysteries of which it will be more fittingly treated in what follows, when the order of reading reaches the middle and third upper room. Thirty cubits. On account of the faith of the Trinity, in the vision of which all the desires of our hope are suspended. Single numbers are multiplied by ten, because through faith and keeping of the law patience is wholesomely exercised: charity burns manfully, and hope is raised sublimely to eternal things. In height. Height signifies the hope of future reward, for which one scorns prosperity or adversity until he sees the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
6.3: 6.3 There was a porch, etc. About this it is written thus in Chronicles: The porch before the front, which extended in length according to the measure of the breadth of twenty cubits, II Chronicles 3. It is clear therefore that this porch was made on the eastern side of the temple. For the temple faced east, like the tabernacle: and it had a door on the east opposite the door of the temple, according to Josephus, so that the rising equinoctial sun, with straight lines of rays through the three doors, of the porch, namely, of the temple and of the oracle, flooded the ark of the covenant. The temple figures the Church; the porch, which before the temple first received the light of the sun, that part of the Church which preceded the incarnation of the Lord: in which the patriarchs and prophets first received the rising sun of righteousness, and gave testimony to the Lord being born in the flesh by living, preaching, being born, and dying. Twenty cubits of length, according to the measure of the breadth of the temple. BEDE, book on the Temple of Solomon, chapter 6. Because the just of old waited in patience and longsuffering, etc., down to yet could not hear his teaching and receive the sacraments.
6.4: 6.4 Slanting windows. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 7. The holy teachers, to whom, when they are carried out of themselves into God, it is granted to see the secrets of heavenly things more specially. They, while they openly set forth what they see in secret, like windows that have received the light of the sun fill all the inner places of the temple. Hence they are said to be slanting, that is wider within: because he who perceives the radiance of heavenly contemplation, even for a moment, soon enlarges the bosom of his heart by chastening it more, and prepares it by skillful exercise to take in greater things.
6.5: 6.5 And he built, etc. THE SAME, ibid. These storeys are called in the Gospel, where the Lord is tempted by the devil, the pinnacles of the temple, etc., down to most of whom the history of St Stephen testifies more fully to have left their wives, where it calls women of the same religion not wives, but their widows. Sides. THE SAME, ibid. That is little turrets, lest anyone should easily fall from there to the lower places, etc., down to Sides, that is walls or railings or little turrets, teachers sitting in the storeys, who preached to the people standing below.
6.6: 6.6 And he laid beams in the house round about on the outside. BEDE, ibid. The houses which carry the storeys, etc., down to and yet from those things which they show outwardly by speaking, doing or suffering, we find help of salvation. Beams, etc., on the outside. They were of such length that their ends projected outside. In the lowest row seven cubits, in the middle six, in the top five, so that the storeys were laid on their ends, not fixed in the walls of the temple, but laid on beams that came out from the walls beside the walls.
6.7: 6.7 But the house, etc. This pertains properly to that part of the Church which after the labors and struggles of the age has merited to be brought in to eternal rewards. For nothing unclean shall enter into that city. And hammer and axe. Because here we are beaten by adversities and exercised by the discipline of truth, that there we may be arranged in fitting places according to merit, and with chastisement ceasing, by the sole glue of love by which we are joined to one another, filled with one spirit we may be steeped. But although it is said: Noah a perfect man in his generations, and: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, and the like, no one can truly walk the way of this life perfect and without stain. For there is none who does good and does not sin. But according to the manner of this time they are called perfect and undefiled, who are then truly made perfect when, released from the bonds of the body, they have come to the immortal beauty of the house of the Lord.
6.8: 6.8 The door of the side. BEDE, ibid., chapter 8. Some, badly understanding this place, etc., down to and well one door, on account of the harmonious faith and love of truth in all the saints. They went up into the middle upper room and from the middle into the third. And he built. BEDE, ibid. Note that the thirty cubits of height, of which one reads above, etc., down to because with harmonious mind and voice all will praise the glory of the divine majesty.
6.9: 6.9 Ceilings. BEDE, ibid., chapter 9. The ceilings are boards, which, put together and adorned with great beauty, are fixed from the lower part to the beams, and since the house of the Lord was made of three heights, it had three ceilings. For the higher saints, namely, whose work and teaching set before all in the temple stand out as if higher up; who by interceding, exhorting, protect the souls of the weak lest they fail. Of cedar. THE SAME, ibid. The cedar is an incorruptible tree, etc., down to unless to love God with the whole heart, whole soul, whole strength, and our neighbor as ourselves.
6.10: 6.10 A floor over the whole house of five cubits in height. BEDE, ibid. Here the topmost roof of the house itself is spoken of, etc., down to in the spirit and power of Elijah.
6.15: 6.15 And he built the walls. BEDE, ibid. Within the house was clothed with cedar, etc., down to but they have none to carry. The walls of the house. They are covered when the hearts of the faithful overflow with love of virtues. For as cedar signifies the perfect, so in suitable places the loftiness of virtues, by which one arrives at the same perfection. From the pavement. All is covered with wood, from the pavement of the house to the top of the walls and up to the ceilings, when the elect from the first rudiments of faith to the perfection of good action, and to the entrance of the heavenly homeland, sweat at good works, when from the first just to the last at the consummation of the age all strive after virtues, by whose merit they dare to say: We are the good odor of Christ to God, II Corinthians 2. And he covered the pavement. BEDE, ibid. This is more fully written in Chronicles, etc., down to he added: But above all things having charity, etc., I Timothy 1; Colossians 3.
6.16: 6.16 He built twenty. BEDE, ibid., chapter 10. That the storeys, etc., down to and this through the whole breadth of the Church spread through the world.
6.17: 6.17 Moreover. THE SAME, ibid. Ten taken four times makes forty, etc., down to but the world is square, in which we strive to acquire the same. Hence: He gathered them from the regions. From the rising and the setting of the sun, from the north and the sea, Psalm 106.
6.18: 6.18 And with cedar all. Cedar signifies the invincible beauty of virtues, with which wood the whole house is clothed within, when the hearts of the just shine with love of good works alone. Having carvings. BEDE, ibid., chapter 11. The house has its carvings and fitted joints in its cedar boards when the elect are bound to one another by the most beautiful bond of charity, that they may have one heart and one soul. For the carvings that are set against the joints of the boards, so that one board is made of all, are the offices of charity by which holy brotherhood is joined and compacted into one house of Christ in the whole world. Engravings. The works of the saints set forth in plain expression what they are as an example to others. Hence Paul sets himself forth as an example both in deeds and words. All of cedar, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The stones of the wall or pavement, and the boards, and the gold, etc., down to and those who have perfectly received the grace of the Gospel equally enjoy eternal life.
6.19: 6.19 The oracle. BEDE, ibid. The oracle where the ark was, etc., down to who after the resurrection ascending into heaven placed the flesh taken of the virgin at the right hand of the Father.
6.20: 6.20 And the oracle. Well is the inner house twenty cubits long, for the mystery of twofold love, of which it has already been spoken, which in this life illumines in the greatest part the minds of the elect, but in the homeland, the works of other virtues ceasing, reigns alone. But also the altar. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 12. Of incense, namely, etc., down to what stone, cedar, and gold signify has been said above.
6.21: 6.21 And the house before the oracle. BEDE, ibid. The house before the oracle is covered with gold, etc., down to hence: I will love him and will manifest myself to him. And again: The hour comes when I shall no longer speak to you in proverbs, etc., John 14; 16. Golden nails. THE SAME, ibid. The nails are the precepts of charity, etc., down to who again, coming to perfection, says of the nails of love: But it is good for me to cling to God, etc., Psalm 118, 72.
6.22: 6.22 And there was nothing in the temple. THE SAME, ibid. These things are more fully explained in Chronicles, II Chronicles 3., etc., down to and think on the things that are above, not on the things on earth, Colossians 3.
6.23: 6.23 Cherubim of wood. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 13. It is a name of angelic dignity, and is said in the singular cherub, in the plural cherubim. By cherubim therefore the angelic ministries which always stand by the Creator in heaven can be understood
6.24: 6.24 Of five cubits. THE SAME, ibid. Wings, when they are put in the figure of holy men, etc., down to which is promised to the cultivators of life, they come to the denarius. One wing of the cherub. They have two wings, because the testaments declare that through prosperity and adversity with unwearied purpose they have always aimed at and reached heavenly things, because they show that the same is to be done by their hearers.
6.25: 6.25 Also of ten cubits. BEDE, ibid. They are ten cubits high, because they preach that God is to be served by observing the Decalogue, because they show that those who serve God faithfully are to be rewarded with the denarius of the eternal kingdom. THE SAME, ibid. And the work. Two cherubim were made to signify the fellowship of charity, etc., down to to whom after the cold and darkness of idolatry it is given to know the light of truth. THE SAME, ibid. By the two cherubim the two Testaments can be figured, etc., down to but because the festivity of interior blessedness is greater from the fellowship of united brotherhood. In the midst of the inner temple. THE SAME, ibid. It is clear from what was said, etc., down to expresses that grace of love by which they embrace one another.
6.27: 6.27 And they stretched out their wings, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The cherubim stretch their wings to either wall of the oracle, etc., down to their writers, now reigning with the Lord and praising him, take care for our salvation, interceding for us.
6.28: 6.28 And he covered the cherubim. They are surrounded with gold, because by the splendid works of their writers the authority of the testaments is confirmed, and the knowledge of the divine Scriptures is made manifest throughout the world, or the inner glory of the heavenly hosts. For cherubim signifies both, namely both angels and testaments.
6.29: 6.29 He carved with various engravings. BEDE, ibid., chapter 14. The walls are carved by the lathe, etc., down to which exercised by long use of virtues it has learned. And palm trees. THE SAME, ibid. He makes palm trees when he fixes the memory of eternal reward in the minds of the saints, that they may fall the less from the ark of righteousness the more they have the reward of righteousness always before their eyes. And various pictures. He makes various pictures, as if projecting from the wall and coming out, when he bestows on the faithful all the manifold workings of virtues, namely the bowels of mercy, kindness, humility, patience, modesty, etc., and above all charity, which is the bond of perfection, Colossians 3. These virtues, when they have come in the elect to such habit that they seem naturally implanted, what else are they than as pictures of the house of the Lord projecting from the wall? Because the words and works of truth they do not yet learn from others outwardly, but fixed in themselves at the root they always bring forth, ready from the depths of the heart, what is to be done or taught. We said that the evenness of the pavement signifies the humble concord of brotherhood: where, though there are Jews or Gentiles, barbarians and Scythians, free and slaves, noble and ignoble, all glory that they are brothers in Christ and have the same Father in heaven. For the most concordant humility of the heavenly citizens is doubtful to no one. Solomon therefore covered the pavement of the house with gold in the oracle within, and in the temple without: because Christ filled angels and the souls of the just in heaven with the full gift of perfection, and separated the pilgrim citizens of the heavenly homeland in the world, by the eternal seal of love, from the vileness of mortals. Hence: By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another, John 13.
6.31: 6.31 And at the entrance of the oracle, etc. BEDE, ibid., chapter 15. There was one entrance, but it was shut by two doors, etc., down to indeed all the elect open for themselves the entrance of the heavenly homeland by the arms of light and of piety. Two little doors of olive wood. THE SAME, ibid. There are two little doors, because angels and holy men love God and neighbor, and cannot enter the gate of life except by the twofold love. Or because for the faithful of both peoples, namely Jews and Gentiles, the same gate of life is opened. And the posts of the corners. They have posts of five corners, because the heavenly hall receives not only the souls of the elect but also opens its doors in the judgment to bodies endowed with immortal glory, for there are five senses of the body. Or each post of the oracle is five cubits high, because the entrance to the heavenly homeland is opened only to those who serve the Lord with all the senses of body and heart: of the body, namely when through them they do something for that; of the heart, when they think soberly and justly and piously of what they resolve to do through the very senses of the body.
6.32: 6.32 Reliefs. It could be called carving made in the joint of the boards, but it is taken broadly. BEDE, ibid. Anaglypha in Greek, in Latin they are called engravings, etc., down to by looking at these we continually direct our steps.
6.33: 6.33 And he made at the entrance. As the entrance of the oracle, by which one comes to the ark of the Lord and the cherubim, signifies the entrance of heaven, by which we desire to be brought in to the vision of God and of the heavenly citizens: so the entrance into the temple signifies the beginnings of our conversion to God, when we enter the present Church. This one designates our entrance to faith, that one to hope. Hence the posts of this entrance are four-sided on account of the four books of the Gospel, by whose teaching we are instructed in the faith of truth. Posts of wood. BEDE, ibid. Four-cornered on account of the four principal virtues, etc., down to the fourth after prudence, fortitude and temperance, justice follows.
6.34: 6.34 On either side. Because they look at one another, so that one cannot be had without the other. The outer door is brotherly love, the inner divine: because that is prior in time, this higher in dignity: and through that this is entered: because in love of neighbor we learn how the Creator ought to be loved. And both doors. BEDE, ibid. Because in each love two things are chiefly to be observed, etc., down to because, all sins being extinguished, we pass to the shore and the firmness of virtues. BEDE, as above. Note that at the exit of the oracle two doors are said to have been, etc., down to prefiguring another dispensation of the mystery. And one another. Or the door which held one another is opened when through the ministry of the preacher it is discerned what properly pertains to the knowledge of faith and what to the chastity of living, both of which cannot be separated, and that it is little to bear the evils of neighbors and not lend them good things, since these are most surely wont to remain indissolubly in the heart of the perfect.
6.35: 6.35 And he carved cherubim. These have been explained above, because on the walls of the house and on the inner doors the same pictures or engravings were made; because the same secrets of faith, hope, and charity, which the sublime and perfect grasp sublimely, and which all the elect fully receive in the eternal vision, are also handed on to be learned and confessed by the uninstructed catechumens each according to his capacity, that, initiated in the sacred mysteries, they may at some time come to grasp what they have piously believed.
6.36: 6.36 He built the court. BEDE as above, chapter 16. He speaks briefly of the inner court, etc., down to whence follows: He built the inner court with three rows, I Corinthians 2. And one row. One row of cedar timbers is good work done without corruption of pretense, without the addition of which faith, hope, and charity cannot be true. For cedar wood, on account of the grace of its odor and the unrotting power of its nature, designates perseverance and the fame of pious action. As far as this court all the elect ascend, who by faith, hope, charity, and work seek to please God, this the perfect pass beyond by the high grace of merits, when they advance to such a height of virtues that they can say to their hearers: Be imitators of me as I am of Christ, I Corinthians 4; and: Do you not know that we shall judge angels, how much more worldly things? ibid. 6.
6.38: 6.38 This is the month. BEDE as above. The question is how the house of the Lord is said to have been perfected in the eighth month in all its work, etc., down to hence David entitled a Psalm for the eighth, which he sang for fear of judgment, saying: O Lord, rebuke me not in your fury, nor chastise me in your wrath, Psalm 6. And he built it. Because the Church through the whole time of this age, which is run by a circuit of seven days, is built of elect souls: and at the end of the age brings its growth to its end. Or on account of the signification of spiritual grace, through which the Church receives that it be a Church: because without the gifts of the Spirit no one can become faithful, or keep the faith, or by the merit of faith come to the crown of righteousness.
7.1: 7.1 But the house of the woman. BEDE, book on the Temple of Solomon, chapter 17. Of the Church, namely the present one, for which Christ her husband, having tasted death, rose, etc., down to For bronze is very durable and sonorous.
7.14: 7.14 He did all the work. Because holy teachers, while they faithfully attend to the ministry of the word, work the work of God, because by speaking outwardly they open the way of truth to those whom he himself by illuminating within has predestined to eternal life. Hence: I planted, Apollos watered, but the Lord gave the increase, II Corinthians 3.
7.15: 7.15 And he cast. BEDE as above, chapter 18. The column before the doors of the temple is eighteen cubits high, etc., down to lest we turn aside in any part from the right way by which we go to the promised homeland. Ten, etc. For three times six makes eighteen: three, namely, pertain to faith on account of the Trinity; six to work, because the world was made in six days, three multiplied by six, when the just man lives by faith and heaps up knowledge of pious faith by the performance of good action. And a line. BEDE, ibid. The rule of apostolic institution encircles each column, when the teacher sent to preach to Jews or Gentiles takes care to do and teach only what the Church has received and learned through the apostles. For he who wishes to teach, live, or preach otherwise, and to despise apostolic decrees or set up new ones at his pleasure, is not a column in the temple of God: because while he scorns to follow apostolic institutions, whether by the thinness of idleness or the grossness of pride he does not fit the line of twelve cubits.
7.16: 7.16 Two, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The capitals of the columns, etc., down to the grace of evangelical perfection is implanted.
7.17: 7.17 Seven, etc. THE SAME, ibid. This is thus written in Chronicles, etc., down to because the fathers of both testaments received, through the grace of one sevenfold Spirit, that they might be elect.
7.18: 7.18 And two. THE SAME. The pomegranates seem to have been made around the capitals from the lower part, and from the pomegranates themselves the nets to arise: by which the capitals were in part covered, it is signified that virtues are born of virtues, and that the saints go from virtue to virtue, Psalm 83. THE SAME, ibid. There were two rows of nets around the capital, etc., down to and in those things which we understand it extends widely. That they might cover. THE SAME, ibid. Since it has been said of the nets, etc., down to it is fittingly added: But the capitals which were above the heads of the columns, etc. Of the pomegranates. Which enclose many grains within with one rind outside, etc., down to but what is within, the grace of faith, hope, and love, and of the other goods of the soul, is not seen.
7.19: 7.19 As, etc. THE SAME, ibid. By lilies is designated the brightness of the heavenly homeland and the delightfulness of paradise fragrant with flowers of immortality, etc., down to because only through the Gospel did that desired voice sound upon the world, Do penance, etc., Matthew 3. In the porch. Note in this saying of Chronicles that the same porch of the temple is also called the vestibule of the temple. Hence: Between the vestibule and the altar they wept; that is, between the porch and the altar.
7.20: 7.20 And again, BEDE as above. Whose making, namely, designates the height of the eternal kingdom, etc., down to but because that fellowship is given to the faithful of both peoples, rightly is added: Of the pomegranates. THE SAME, ibid. In the pomegranate he signifies the whole Church, etc., down to and gather the elect of both peoples in one citadel of blessedness. Column. THE SAME, ibid. The right column signifies the teachers of the primitive Church, etc., down to nothing of effort at least to understand the errors of those over whom they are set. He also made. THE SAME, ibid. This sea was made as a figure of baptism, etc., down to when he foretold that this was to be given to those laboring in the vineyard.
7.23: 7.23 From brim to brim. Because from the first baptized in the name of Jesus Christ to the last who at the end of the age will believe and be baptized, the whole choir of the faithful must enter the same way of truth, and hope from the Lord the common crown of righteousness. Of five cubits. Because whatever we offend in sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch, the grace of God releases to us through the washing of the life-giving fountain. But forgiveness of past sins does not suffice unless one thereafter strives at good works; otherwise the devil who had gone out of the man, if he sees him idle from good works, returns more manifold, and makes his last state worse than the first; hence it is added: And a line of thirty cubits encircled it. The discipline of heavenly precepts by which we are bound back from pleasures; hence: A threefold cord is not easily broken, Ecclesiastes 4, because the observance of the commandments which is established in the hearts of the elect by faith, love, and hope of the heavenly reward can be dissolved by no obstacle. The line encircles the sea, when we strive to fortify with pious works the sacrament of baptism which we have received. This is of thirty cubits, for five times six makes thirty. By the number six, in which the Lord made man when he was not, and remade him when he had perished, our good working is figured. And six is multiplied by five, to reach thirty, when all the senses of the body are subjected to divine commands. Otherwise: three times ten makes thirty, and the human race after the flood, from the offspring of the three sons of Noah, filled the breadth of the whole world. Shem indeed obtained Asia, Ham Africa, the offspring of Japheth Europe and the islands of the sea. And because the mystery of baptism, with the performance of works and hope of heavenly things, was to be ministered to all nations, the line of thirty cubits encircled the sea in which baptism was figured. But also here it must be said that the Lord, when he was thirty years old, came to baptism, who, since by his baptism which he received at thirty he consecrated our baptism, rightly was the sea, which figured our baptism, encircled by a cord of thirty cubits, that it might be signified that by the gift of him who underwent baptism without sin, baptism is dedicated to us believing in him for the remission of sins. And carving. Since it has been said that a line of thirty cubits encircled the sea, and now it is added that this carving placed under the brim encircled it by ten cubits, it is clear that the vessel was spread out and diffused in the manner of a bowl, which from the thirty cubits of circuit which it had at the brim was drawn in to ten. A carving is storied which imitates some histories of things. Hence by the storied carvings with which the sea is surrounded are signified the examples of former times, which are to be looked at by us, that we may see by what works the saints from the beginning pleased God, with what obstinacy the wicked persevered in crimes, with how great misfortune the reprobate perished. As in the beginning of the nascent world Cain was condemned for the malice of envy, Abel crowned by merit of righteousness, Lamech cursed for adultery and homicide, Enoch led back to paradise for grace of piety, Ham after the flood detested for impiety, Shem and Japheth given perpetual blessing for the service of reverence, Abraham by merit of faith made heir of the divine promise, the rest of the multitude of nations left for unbelief. And at the coming of the Lord in the flesh, Judea rejected for unfaithfulness, the Gentiles led back by grace to salvation, and such things, which carefully considered in both testaments profit the studious. Therefore perhaps there are two rows of storied carvings on the bronze sea, that those who are steeped in the font of baptism may listen to the histories of both testaments: therefore they were of ten cubits in the circuit, that whomever they see in those histories devoted to obeying heavenly commands, and suspended with all their intent upon heavenly rewards, they may strive to imitate.
7.25: 7.25 Twelve. BEDE as above. The apostle, the evangelists, indeed all ministers of the word; hence: You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the grain, etc., I Corinthians 9. These carry the sea placed upon them, when the apostles and their successors fulfill with ready devotion the office of the Gospel enjoined on them. Of whom three. Because in all parts of the four-sided world they preach the faith of the Trinity. Hence also twelve apostles, that is four times three, were chosen, that evangelizing the faith and confession of the Trinity through the four quarters of the world they might baptize all nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Whose words, deeds, and sufferings, and those of their successors, we can readily see and know now by reading. But what glory of retribution awaits them in the future we cannot yet see.
7.26: 7.26 Thickness. BEDE as above. He who receives the bath of baptism for salvation and life ought to have faith and hope and charity, without which no one can work rightly; hence it is added, Thickness. Because the reception of baptism is fortified by the strength of faith, hope, and charity, and is not shown to be profitable to those receiving it unless the firm certainty of these virtues strengthens the mind and body of the recipients. Of a lily. THE SAME, ibid. The lily, with the grace of its accompanying scent, a white color outwardly, etc., down to hence it is added: It held two thousand baths and three thousand, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The bath is a measure of the Hebrews, etc., down to makes them partakers of the same kingdom.
7.27: 7.27 THE SAME, ibid. A thousand signifies perfection, because ten makes a solid square. For ten times ten makes a hundred, which is a figure now square, but still flat. But to rise in height and be made solid, multiply a hundred by ten, and it makes a thousand. By this number the stable and as it were squared conscience of the just is signified. For wherever you throw a square, it will stand, so the mind of the elect is bent from the state of uprightness by no temptation. And he made. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 20. In many ways and by many means the same sacraments of our salvation are figured, etc., down to made to glow with divine love. THE SAME, ibid. That ten bases were made to carry the lavers, etc., down to but invoking God the Father by one and the same name for the gift of the one Spirit. Of four cubits in length. THE SAME, ibid. The length and breadth of the bases were of four cubits each, because preachers, whether they bear outwardly the adversities of the world and the length of exile and present labors, or enlarge the heart in the love of God and neighbor by inner exultation, always strive after virtues, discerning prudently between good and evil, bearing adversities with fortitude, tempering the heart from desire of pleasures, holding justice in action.
7.28: 7.28 And the work of the bases itself. The tablets of which the bases were made were square, in which were round moldings, which are called little crowns or plaits, in the middle of which were carvings of lions, etc.
7.29: 7.29 Between the little crowns and the plaits, lions and oxen and cherubim. THE SAME, ibid. There was no surface of the bases flat on any side, etc., down to hence here also after the carvings of cherubim it is well added: And beneath the lions. Because teachers, both in the severity of strictness by which they judge sinners and in the mildness of gentleness by which they forgive the penitent, fear the judgment of God, lest binding and loosing unjustly they be justly bound by him whose judgment cannot err.
7.30: 7.30 And four wheels. BEDE, ibid. The four books of the Gospels, etc., down to they lift them from the bottom and as if with wheels fitted raise the bases higher from the ground by their axles. Little shoulders. THE SAME, ibid. Which, set before the wheels, stood in the way that they could not slip from the axle, are the proclamations of the prophets, by which the evangelical and apostolic Scripture is confirmed, lest it come into doubt to any reader; hence: We have the more sure prophetic word, to which you do well to attend, etc., II Peter 1. Hence also Mark says: The beginning of the Gospel of the Son of God as it is written in Isaiah the prophet; and Matthew: Now all this was done that the Scripture of the prophets might be fulfilled, Mark 1; Matthew 26. Against. THE SAME, ibid. Because all prophetic Scripture is in agreement with itself, as composed by one spirit. There were four little shoulders on each base, according to the number of the wheels, not that there are only four prophetic books, but all that the prophets spoke bore witness to the four Gospels, that from the consent of both Testaments one faith and love of Christ might strengthen the hearts of us all.
7.31: 7.31 One cubit. THE SAME, ibid. On account of perfection, etc., down to hence: For we know in part and we prophesy in part, etc., I Corinthians 13. Middle. He says the upper tablet, which like the others was square and similarly carved, and at its top had a roundness of one and a half cubits, in which the laver was placed.
7.37: 7.37 In this manner he made ten bases, one casting, and measure, and carving, etc. BEDE, ibid. Why ten bases were made and as many lavers set under, has been said above; but that there was one measure and carving alike for all the bases or lavers was not done with this meaning, that the merits of all the teachers can be equal; but because they have one faith of the Gospel by which they are instructed, one sacrament of baptism by which they are washed, one and the same Spirit by whom all are consecrated, though they have diverse gifts in the same Spirit, who divides to each as he wills.
7.38: 7.38 One laver held forty baths, etc. THE SAME, ibid. Forty signifies great perfection, because four times ten makes forty, and ten are the precepts by which all our working is bounded in the law of God. And the four books of the Gospels, in which through the dispensation of the Lord's incarnation the entrance to the heavenly homeland has been laid open to us, and because all who belong to the mystery of baptism, with the faith and sacraments of the Gospel, ought to show the fruit of right action, each of the lavers in which the burnt offerings were washed held forty baths. And it was. THE SAME, ibid. That which was said above: and it likewise had one cubit and a half, and whether he signified there breadth or height, he did not add: it seems that he meant the bottom of this laver to be understood of this breadth, which is easily conjectured from the measure of the base on which each laver was placed, which is thus described: At the top of the base there was a certain roundness of one and a half cubits, so made that the laver could be placed on it. The breadth of the bottom in the lavers therefore was one cubit and a half. But the capacity of the lavers had four cubits, but whether in height, or in breadth, or in both, let him say who knows. THE SAME, ibid. On account of the four Gospels in which the form of baptism, or on account of the cardinal virtues by which the baptized ought to be formed, or on account of the four quarters of the world in which baptism is ministered.
7.39: 7.39 And he set the ten bases, five on the right side of the temple, and five on the left. THE SAME, ibid. But the right side of the temple and the left not inside the temple itself, etc., down to and I consider the flame of divine charity to be foreign. But the sea he put at the right side of the temple, etc. THE SAME, ibid. And in this same court, etc., down to through which the same love is poured out in our hearts.
7.46: 7.46 The king cast them in the plain of Jordan. THE SAME, ibid. In which our Lord was baptized, etc., down to he filled through the whole breadth of the world. Clay ground. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 21. Of which the molds were made for casting the vessels of Scripture, etc., down to that by running well we may reach their rewards.
7.48: 7.48 And Solomon made all the vessels in the house, etc. THE SAME, ibid. Above he said Hiram made for Solomon all the vessels, now Scripture adds that Solomon made the same. For Solomon made by dictating, Hiram by working. The golden altar. THE SAME, ibid. The hearts of the perfect shine with the light of inner charity and chastity, etc., down to but only offer him vows of tears and prayer for desire of the heavenly kingdom. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 22. Moses made the altar of incense, etc., down to hence those who labor in the vineyard of the great householder are reckoned by the denarius. The table. THE SAME, ibid. Scripture, clear by spiritual understanding, etc., down to which was once thought to be understood according to the letter. THE SAME, ibid. As tables are put as a type of Scripture, etc., down to so the elect are contained in Scripture; with their sense raised to the heights they seek and receive heavenly goods from the Lord.
7.49: 7.49 As of a lily. THE SAME, ibid. He seems to say this because the highest part of the candlesticks was formed in the manner of an opened lily. Golden lamps above. By which what contains is meant for what it contains, that is the little golden vessels in which the oil burned. Tongs. BEDE, ibid. That is, snuffers with which the wicks were snuffed, that being renewed they might burn better.
7.50: 7.50 Water jars. The water jars signify the hearts of the saints, filled with the water of wisdom and the wine of compunction. Forks. The forks with which meats are prepared, preachers, who administer to their hearers the food of understanding: whose office is to distribute the body and blood of Christ to believers, to deny them to unbelievers. Of the inner house. THE SAME, ibid., chapter 22. The doors of the inner house are angelic, etc., down to or that which they have of charity toward God.
7.51: 7.51 He finished all the work. THE SAME, ibid. While the state of the age goes on, he does indeed do the work of the house of the Lord, but does not yet finish it, because the Lord inspires and helps the hearts of the elect to do good; yet he grants that no one dwelling in this life is without sin. For this he reserves for future blessedness. But he finishes all the work of the temple of Solomon and makes it fit for dedication when our peaceful one on the last day glorifies the elect with the immortality of the resurrection and leads them to the eternal kingdom. Hence the temple was built in seven years, but in the eighth finished and dedicated. With which time agrees what follows: And he brought in the things which he had sanctified. THE SAME, ibid. David, the father of Solomon, had sanctified silver when God the Father strengthens those who speak with the grace of his Spirit to speak the word of God. He sanctifies gold when he illumines those endowed with natural wit to understand the law. He sanctifies also vessels when he bestows the grace of the Holy Spirit on all the children of the Church. These sanctified things Solomon brings into the temple when the Lord, the judgment completed, brings the company of teachers and other faithful into the joy of the heavenly kingdom. And he put them in the treasuries of the house of the Lord. THE SAME, ibid. Because he hides his own in the hiding place of his face from the disturbance of men. There are many treasuries in one house of the Lord, because in one Church the saints differ in merits. And the heavenly homeland is one, though in it star differs from star in brightness, II Corinthians 15. Both of which the distributor of rewards showed when he said: In my Father's house are many mansions, John 15.
8.6: 8.6 Into the holy place. BEDE, book on the Temple of Solomon. The outer house of the temple designates the pilgrim Church, the holy of holies the heavenly happiness of the supernal homeland. The ark brought into the holy of holies, the humanity of Christ taken up, led within the veil of the heavenly court. Under the wings. THE SAME. Moses made two golden cherubim, which he placed on the mercy seat which was over the ark. Solomon added two larger, under whose wings the ark is now said to have been placed with the mercy seat and the two earlier cherubim.
8.8: 8.8 And when. THE SAME. This more clearly, etc., down to if the bars projecting beyond the door gave no place for drawing out to shut the doors. Which also were. It is said in Chronicles: The ark was there until the present day: which was added by the historian, signifying that until the times of his age it remained there, which cannot be understood of Ezra, because the temple was already burned, but of Nathan or one of the prophets, by whom all the deeds of their times are believed to have been written.
8.9: 8.9 In the ark. RABANUS. There was in the ark a golden urn having manna, etc., down to because only the citizens of the heavenly homeland fully contemplate there the glory of the Redeemer.
8.10: 8.10 A cloud filled the house of the Lord, and they could not. THE SAME. That is, it filled the synagogue, because the darkness of unbelief filled their minds, and the priests could not minister because of the cloud, because while they disdain to investigate the mystical senses covered by the veil of the letter and the sacraments of Christ's nativity, they lost through the cloud of error the ministry due to their faith, so that, as their merits demand, they do not acknowledge the worship of belief, to whom in the cloud of his teaching the Lord told even plain things about himself. But because the darkness of unbelief had filled the minds of the hearers, as an intervening cloud hides a sent-out ray of the sun.
8.55: 8.55 He stood. In Chronicles it is related what is not said here: Solomon had made a bronze platform and set it in the middle of the court, standing on which he blessed all the assembly of Israel. And he blessed. RABANUS. The temple of the Lord, etc., down to and by works of virtue benefit their neighbors.
8.64: 8.64 On that day. RABANUS, in the book of Kings, volume 3. What is it that Solomon built the middle of the court, offering there, etc., down to acceptable sacrifices are offered to God spiritually every day. Altar. That which Moses made was set before the temple facing its doors, and because it was narrow and could not hold, he sanctified the middle of the court under the open sky, where he put that very great altar which he had made of twenty cubits.
8.65: 8.65 The feast. RABANUS as above. In Chronicles, etc., down to which Josephus also attests. THE SAME, ibid. The solemnity which Solomon made and all Israel, etc., down to which in Christ the Father conferred on Christians. From the entrance. RABANUS, ibid. By the entrance of Hamath he designates the northern quarter of Judea, by the river or brook of Egypt the southern. This river is not the Nile, but another river which flows into the sea near Rhinocolura. Hamath is a city of Syria. Now it is called Epiphania from Antiochus Epiphanes.
8.66: 8.66 Rejoicing. Singing hymns with delight, so that in that pleasantness without labor they returned to their own.
9.11: 9.11 Furnishing the king. RABANUS as above. Much gold and silver, etc., down to because they did not bring forth the shoot with fullness of fruits.
9.17: 9.17 He built. RABANUS. The cities which he is said to have built, etc., down to that they may be unconquerable by spiritual enemies. RABANUS. The cities which Solomon built were of the remnants of the Amorites, which the children of Israel could not destroy, as is read in Joshua, Joshua 9: these afterward the king of Egypt overthrew and gave as dowry to his daughter, wife of Solomon, and therefore Solomon rebuilt them.
9.18: 9.18 And Palmyra. An uninhabitable region because nowhere was water found; but in that place where the city is built, springs abound, and palms, which in Greek are called Palmira, it is Hamath itself, or Epiphania or Antioch.
9.20: 9.20 All the people. RABANUS as above. Those who were not of the children of Israel our Peaceful One made tributary, with those who are not in the number of sons; but he uses them in servile condition for his own service. Such, though in many things they oppose, yet often serve the uses of the Church, when in the present time they afford comforts from their goods. Of the children. THE SAME, ibid. Those who are not sons of the slave woman, but of the free, etc., down to and lead into the paths of righteousness.
9.23: 9.23 Fifty. THE SAME. On the fiftieth day after Passover both the law was given on Mount Sinai and the Spirit the Paraclete came upon the disciples. What then does this number of overseers signify, except that those who by the grace of the Holy Spirit merit to have knowledge of the law of the Lord are themselves able to rule well both themselves and others?
9.25: 9.25 He also offered. THE SAME. Our Peaceful One offers, etc., down to and asks what is pleasing to God.
9.26: 9.26 A fleet. THE SAME. The fleet is the Church, etc., down to history, allegory, tropology, anagoge in the two Testaments.
9.28: 9.28 To Ophir. THE SAME. Ophir is the name of a province in India. It is named from Ophir, one of the descendants of Eber, which is also called the golden land, because it has golden mountains, which are inhabited by lions and very fierce beasts. No one dares approach them otherwise than by standing in a ship near the shore and taking into their ship the earth they find dug up by the claws of the lions, so that if the beasts perceive them, they may easily be received into the sea.
10.1: 10.1 Allegorically. ISIDORE, in the book of Kings, volume 5. This queen signifies the Church to come from the Gentiles, etc., down to desiring to become a fellow citizen of the saints in secret.
10.4: 10.4 And seeing. RABANUS as above. The queen, having seen Solomon and his glory, amazed at his prudence, said: The word is true, etc. So holy Church, having heard the miracles of Christ, is provoked to seek him: whom having found by faith, considering the testimonies of holy Scripture, recognizing the power of his divinity, she thinks all that was told her about him before to be little.
10.8: 10.8 Blessed are your men. RABANUS. The queen, in admiration, burst into praise of Solomon, saying: Blessed are your men. Truly blessed are those whose king is Christ, and who merit to enjoy his eternal vision, and rejoice to behold the glory which he has with the Father and the Holy Spirit and to receive forever the wisdom which he shows to the pure in heart.
10.11: 10.11 Woods. THE SAME. Our Maker brings precious woods, that is, etc., down to and all instruments of musicians.
10.12: 10.12 For singers. THE SAME. These, whatever they do in word or work, do all for the praise of God: they cease not to proclaim praise in adversity and prosperity, with heart, mouth, and deed, hence: Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen, all the day and night they shall never cease to praise the name of the Lord, Isaiah 62.
10.13: 10.13 And the king. THE SAME. Our Peaceful One too will give to his Church all that she asks, hence: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you. He bestows not only what we ask, but even what human frailty either does not know or does not presume to ask, by free gift.
10.16: 10.16 Two hundred. THE SAME. In Chronicles golden spears are added to the shields, because leaders keeping watch before the door of the king's house used lances and shields. Hence: Sixty valiant men surround the bed of Solomon. THE SAME. Those on guard at the doors of the royal house, etc., down to and with the shield of faith they quench the fiery darts of the wicked one.
10.17: 10.17 The forest of Lebanon. The forest of Lebanon signifies the Church of the Gentiles, which, cut off from the pomp of pride, is fitted into the building of the house of God. Hence: We found her in the fields of the wood.
10.18: 10.18 A throne of ivory. RABANUS. A throne or seat is an imperial chair, which in the Song of Songs is called a litter, because it bears those seated or carries them about from place to place. To which one ascended by six steps. Under the seat was a golden footstool, and the top of the throne was round, held with two hands or arms on the outside, and beside it stood two lions helping to support the seat.
10.20: 10.20 And twelve. Because six steps of ascent were placed on either side to support the stair of the one ascending. THE SAME. The throne of Solomon is understood to be the Church, etc., down to they strive to fortify. It was not made, etc. Aptly this fits the Church, to whom it is said: Many daughters have gathered riches, you have surpassed them all, Proverbs 31.
10.21: 10.21 But also all the vessels, etc. All the vessels that serve the ministry of our Peaceful One are golden, because all the souls of the saints, which are the vessels of God, that they may serve the divine will, shining with the splendor of wisdom and love, contain the drink of life, and there is made in them a fountain of water springing up to eternal life, John 4. Nor of any, etc. RABANUS. Because, according to the Apostle, The kingdom of God is not in word, but in power and the preaching of the Gospel, I Corinthians 1. It does not consist in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in the demonstration of spirit and power, that our faith may be not in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
